narrative:
The model estimated a 68.9% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because that risk was high, your law school application was denied. This is not a judgment that you cannot succeed; it is a risk estimate based on patterns in prior student outcomes. Your gender and race were not used in the prediction.

The strongest factor pushing the prediction toward failure was your third-year grade decile of 2, compared with an average of about 5.79 among accepted students. Your first-year grade decile of 2 was the second strongest factor and also pushed toward failure, versus an average of about 6.00. Together, these early and later academic rankings suggested a persistent pattern of lower relative performance. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.00 was the third most influential factor, and it actually pushed toward passing, although only modestly; it remains slightly below the accepted-student average of about 3.23. It was not enough to offset the two grade-decile signals.

To improve your chances, contact admissions for specific feedback, consider retaking the LSAT if it can be strengthened, and pursue coursework or a graduate credential that demonstrates sustained academic improvement. In a future application, provide context for your early grades and show a clear upward trajectory. Prepare early for bar-exam-style analytical work so your application can address the model’s central concern directly.
